correctness.rationale: At any live state, the probability of reaching the facing endpoint within the next L/v without reversal is at least exp(−K); the Markov property at blocks of length L/v gives a geometric lifetime bound. The outgoing conditions are h_−(0)=0, h_+(L)=1 and m_−(0)=m_+(L)=0 for exit side and time, respectively. Independently solving gives h_+−h_−=p constant and m_+−m_−=τ−2x/v. Integrating h_−'=pλ/v and m_−'=(1+λ(τ−2x/v))/v gives the stated p and τ; at λ=0 the only pair is (1,L/v). For K>0 the centroid B/K is strictly between the endpoints. In the smooth exponential tilt with fixed mass, its derivative with respect to the tilt is L times a strictly positive variance of x/L, and concentration at the two endpoints yields the full open range and sharp unattained edges. A cosine has zero first moment by symmetry about L/2 and zero integral over a period, so small signed perturbations preserve both moments and stay positive on the compact interval; this works for every interior pair, not the deterministic p=1 pair. The supplied simulation uses integrated hazards and bisection, and the archived simulation is only a consistency check; no uploaded code was run.

evidence: The 2014 arbitrary inhomogeneous MFPT formula assumes a reflecting source endpoint, not a pair of absorbing endpoints. The 2015 and 2023 models allow more general wall behavior but use homogeneous bulk reorientation. Malakar et al. §4.2 cover both observables but restrict the bulk rate to a constant.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broadness in the wall classes or noise models does not dominate the freely heterogeneous bulk in the frozen statement; the general inhomogeneous MFPT supplies a different observable, with a usable indirect implication by renewal.

evidence: In the 2014 formula set both speeds to v and both reorientation rates to 2λ, so the integrating factor is one and the integrand in Eq. (5) is v⁻¹[1+2∫_x^L λ(y)/v dy]. Thus T_ref=(L+2B)/v; renewal gives τ=pT_ref. The 2020 backward formulas supply p on the symmetric rate specialization as above. The homogeneous two-observable comparison yields a fixed centroid L/2, not a two-dimensional region.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Both forward identities can be assembled from earlier techniques with the stated boundary conversion. The joint range requires varying mass and centroid independently over the nonnegative continuous rate class, proving strictness and sharpness, and showing exact smooth realization and nonidentifiability. Do not credit the forward identities as isolated new principles.

evidence: Singh–Sabhapandit–Kundu use complementary left-exit probabilities with equivalent outgoing conditions. In their Eq. (76), setting the two rates equal and integrating directly gives the total-rate splitting formula. The one-reflecting-end lifetime T_ref of Angelani–Di Leonardo–Paoluzzi is related by renewal at the left wall: T_ref=τ+(1−p)T_ref.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Changing which exit is counted complements the probability; a reflecting source wall changes the stopping time. The renewal relation, rather than a substitution identifying the two times, explains the overlap. The joint attainable set and exact inverse fibers are the assessed remainder.

originality.rationale: Credit the previously available splitting equations and their direct integrated-rate specialization, as well as the reflecting/absorbing first-passage moment and its renewal relation to τ. The distinct claim assessed is the complete joint feasible region and inverse fibers for the two-absorbing-end injected protocol over arbitrary continuous nonnegative reversal profiles. The checked statements concern pieces, different rate families, or different boundary/start ensembles; no inspected theorem already classifies this joint design problem.
residual_risks: The 2019 space-dependent-speed paper was not available in full for comparison. Related two-stream or inverse-transport literature could encode this joint classification under different terminology; the bounded search does not certify historical priority.

value.rationale: The boundary-injection measurement protocol motivates the simultaneous calibration problem. The sharp feasible region says exactly which pairs of measurements can be matched by a smooth positive rate, and the moment fibers identify what this protocol can and cannot distinguish. These joint feasibility and inverse facts are useful separately from the rather short forward equations; no significance for full exit-time distributions or multi-start measurements is claimed.
